intro: Covers the US session of Monday 23 November (a sharp Nvidia-led rebound after last week's rout). This is the delayed 08:15 edition: closing prints were checked against several sources, but Brent and S&P 500 sector moves could not be verified and are marked "not available".
footnotes: Index closes are from Yahoo Finance quotes cross-checked against Fox Business percentages and the prior Friday closes (S&P 500 6,910.39; Nasdaq 22,617.73; Dow 48,147.33). The Dow's point change differs slightly between sources (+1,447.98 vs +1,450.39).
The VIX is a single-source close (Yahoo); other reports imply 26.8-27.5.
The 10-year yield is from Yahoo; Trading Economics showed a 2 bp fall.
Gold is the Trading Economics spot reference (CFD-based); gold futures were US$3,634.60, +3.39%.
Brent was not available: no verified settlement was found (US crude futures fell about 3.7%).
The iron ore print is dated 20 November, the latest available.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures (December contract) are up about 1.6%, at roughly 8,707-8,717 (range between TradingView and Investing.com; snapshot times unconfirmed, so treat as approximate). Applied to the ASX 200's prior close of about 8,570.6 (-0.26%, an eighth straight daily loss and a six-month low), that implies an open near 8,710, up about 140 points or 1.6%.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian releases or RBA decisions were confirmed for today.
October monthly CPI is due later this week (date unconfirmed; September was 4.3%).
No notable local earnings were identified.
what_moved: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, sending the stock up about 31% and lifting the whole AI and semiconductor complex, in the best session for the three major indexes since April 2025. The S&P 500 recovered more than half of last week's roughly 8.6% plunge and moved out of correction territory; the VIX fell about a quarter. Semiconductors and technology led by a wide margin; S&P 500 sector percentages were not available. Gold rebounded about 3% and US crude fell, while Treasury yields were little changed.

news.headline: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO.
news.summary: The board restored Jensen Huang as CEO, president and chair effective immediately, with President Trump publicly pushing for his return. Nvidia rose about 31%, adding close to US$1 trillion in market value.

news.headline: Wall Street posts its best day since April 2025.
news.summary: The Dow gained about 1,450 points and the Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.5% after a week in which all three indexes entered correction and the Nasdaq had its worst week since 2020.

news.headline: Markets still price a December Fed hike.
news.summary: Futures put the odds of a 25 bp rate rise at the December meeting at about 96%, per CME FedWatch.

news.headline: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler.
news.summary: The US$43.9 billion deal is among the largest cybersecurity takeovers on record.

news.headline: US growth momentum softens.
news.summary: S&P Global's flash PMIs showed US manufacturing growth at a three-month low and services at a four-month low, though both remain above 50.

news.headline: ASX 200 slides to a six-month low.
news.summary: The index fell 0.26% on Monday, its eighth straight daily loss and about 5% lower on the week before, ahead of the overnight rebound.

coming_up: US October PCE inflation is due Wednesday 25 November at 8:30am ET. US markets are closed Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving and close at 1pm ET on Friday 27 November.
